newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBS EDGE UP, SHORT-COVERING DOMINATES IN TOKYO.
newsitem.headline: JGBS EDGE UP, SHORT-COVERING DOMINATES IN TOKYO.

text.p: The benchmark September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract had edged higher by afternoon Tokyo but remained top-heavy, with short-covering activity dominant, traders said.

Light offers were lined up from 126.46-126.50, one city bank trader said. But he added that there were virtually no offers over 126.50, meaning additional gains are possible should the contract rise beyond that level.
"However, positions seem mostly square at this point, so unless we get some fresh buying factors rises are unlikely today," he added.
The key September contract was at 126.42 at 0427 GMT against 126.38 at midday and 126.10 at Wednesday's close.
Yield on the benchmark 182nd 10-year cash bond was at 2.120 percent against 2.155 percent at Wednesday's close, with investor buying of cash bonds lending futures support.
